modifications: Kernels: the routed window is lane L2's own one-token kernels (split gate+up/SwiGLU, served_down = tile4 arithmetic), unchanged, with the token on grid z; the shared-fold window is L2's one-token shared-fold source with the token's pointer offsets substituted (asserted, one occurrence each). omlx's per-format gate+up/down sources and its in-kernel 8-bit shared-gate row are not used (lane L2 measured a 1-ulp miss of that row on 1/36960 calls); the gate logit stays a projection outside the kernel.

Routing matched to mlx2's served stock routing, not to omlx's: omlx's selection is descending with fp32 renormalization (its own router baseline); mlx2's stock argpartition is a stable ascending sort (slot j = selection 9 - j) and the normalization is a sequential bf16 sum over slots then a bf16 divide, both established on Metal (60000 synthetic rows) and reproduced exactly.

router_topk ('launch'): one simdgroup per row, stock-identical routing in one launch, also usable where the routed kernels do not run. 'fold' recomputes the routing in the gate+up launch (every routed simdgroup selects the full ten and takes its slot) at one token and in windows up to topk_fold_max_rows (default 17; omlx 3).

Window projections (router gemv, shared gate, and the shared expert when it is not folded) run through lane L5's row-exact qmv kernel, so every row of the MoE block equals its one-token call; omlx keeps its own router gemv kernel.

Consumers are explicit and separately switched: row-exact verify windows (L5; replaces the per-row routed-expert loop, the window stays row-exact either way), batched one-token decode [B, 1, H], and plain MTP verify windows marked by a model-neutral verify-forward scope. omlx serves the first two only.

Strict admission (split resident tables, tile4 down at width 1, stock or launch routing, no fused router / compiled router / glue / two_launch reference, bf16, 512 experts top-10 normalized, 2..17 rows) with counted, reasoned refusals per consumer; default off (omlx defaults on).
Measured caps: the fold runs at most 3 rows (above: the launch); the batched-decode consumer declines quietly above 8 lanes (B16 was -7%). Both live-settable.
